content.name: Construct-validity v0 (five-axis validity — applies to EVERY construct)
content.lineage: The shared canonical model of what 'valid' means for a construct. Every construct is a self-verifying loop (its validation -> observer -> observer-validation -> metric -> health spine), and this toolkit factors what that spine reports into FIVE orthogonal axes so no single 'health' collapses them. It is consumed by other constructs through DEPENDS_ON; it is not owned by one exclusive toolkit. Promoted from the model first authored in [[space:l2:mind-universe:abstraction-toolkit-v0]].

parent_scope.justification: A shared canonical contract awaiting installation under the sensemaking/meta registry Space. Exactly one scope classification; consumed via DEPENDS_ON, structurally owned by none.

content.native_law_boundary: AtomDynamics knows only AtomSpec, AtomBond and support/inhibit/neutral. This toolkit adds no law; it is a model that reads a construct's own validity spine and reports five orthogonal statuses. The axes and their meanings are data.
content.purpose: Give every construct one shared, canonical way to state its validity as a VECTOR over five orthogonal axes, never a single scalar. A construct DEPENDS_ON this model, and its health face reports one status per axis: (1) causal validity, (2) current truth, (3) degree, (4) scope, (5) context. The axes are independent — a construct may be causally valid yet currently false, currently true yet causally unsound, proven by a weak validator, valid only in scope, or valid only under a context — and each must stay separately visible.

validity_decomposition.note: The canonical five-axis validity model. Any construct that DEPENDS_ON this toolkit reports its health as one status per axis; axes are never collapsed.

causal_validity.question: does the causal/logical structure hold in principle? a-temporal, world-independent
causal_validity.established_by: proof over the causal structure (required arguments conduct, no logical contradiction) — the argument, not the current world

current_truth.question: does it actually hold in the world RIGHT NOW?
current_truth.established_by: fresh runtime evidence read by the observer (a runtime health_assessment)
current_truth.independence: a construct may be causally valid yet currently false, or currently true yet causally unsound

parts.evidence_margin: measured_support minus proof_burden — how far above threshold
parts.validator_strength: the validity AND strength of the validators themselves: is the observer itself proven (observer-validation passing), independent, strong? A pass from a weak or unproven validator is a weak proof.

validity_scope.question: over what domain does it hold? space, time, type/population, scale, revision range
validity_scope.rule: outside the declared scope a construct is OUT-OF-SCOPE, not false; a scope must be declared, never assumed universal

validity_context.question: under what assumptions / preconditions / situation does the above hold?
lives_in: the situation frame: universe revision, active actors, assumed premises
validity_context.rule: distinguish valid-under-context-C from valid-unconditionally; a context change may re-open any of the other four axes

validity_decomposition.collapse_forbidden: No overall health may hide a per-axis defect; each of the five statuses stays separately visible.

content.applies_to: every construct in the Universe, present and future — a construct is a self-verifying loop, and its validity is ALWAYS this five-axis vector. Not a toolkit (a capability like sky/mechanical); the shared validity model itself. Non-construct kernel entities are out of scope.

content.success_condition: Every construct that DEPENDS_ON this toolkit reports its validity as five orthogonal statuses (causal validity, current truth, degree, scope, context), each a faithful projection of measured evidence, with no axis collapsed into another. The five distinguishable cases — causally-valid-but-currently-false, currently-true-but-causally-unsound, proven-by-a-weak-validator, in-scope-only, and conditional-on-context — are always separately visible, and this toolkit itself reports its own validity by the same five axes (it is an instance of the model it defines).

content.pattern: A construct's self-verifying spine (validation -> observer -> observer-validation -> metric -> health, producing validation_run and health_assessment) reports not one scalar but five orthogonal axes. Theoretical/causal validity is read from the pattern/behavior/algorithm as an a-temporal argument; current truth from a fresh health_assessment reading the world; degree from the evidence margin and the validators' own strength and validity; scope from a declared rayon; context from the preconditions and situation frame. The axes are independent and separately statused.
content.epistemic_honesty: A green overall is not permitted to hide a red axis. Out-of-scope is not false. A pass from an unproven validator is weak, not strong. Causal soundness is not current truth, and current truth is not causal soundness.

terms.CausalValidity: Does the causal/logical structure hold in principle? A-temporal, world-independent; read from pattern/behavior/algorithm.
terms.CurrentTruth: Does it hold in the world right now? From a fresh runtime health_assessment.
terms.ValidityDegree: How strong: the evidence margin (support minus burden) AND the validity and strength of the validators themselves.
terms.ValidityScope: The declared domain (space/time/type/scale/revision) over which it holds; out-of-scope is distinct from false.
terms.ValidityContext: The assumptions/preconditions/situation under which the other axes hold.
terms.ValidatorStrength: The validity and strength of a construct's own validators — is the observer proven, independent, strong?
terms.CollapseForbidden: The rule that no single overall status may hide a per-axis defect.
terms.Rayon: The enumerable declared domain of validity_scope.

content.given: A construct (its pattern/behavior/algorithm, its fresh health_assessment, its metric vector, its observer-validation result, a declared scope, and its preconditions/situation frame).
content.when: The construct's health face is derived or refreshed, or an observer inspects the construct's validity.
then: Derive causal_validity from the causal argument (required arguments conducted, no logical contradiction), independent of the current world.
Derive current_truth only from a fresh health_assessment reading the current world.
Derive validity_degree from the evidence margin AND the validators' own strength and validity.
Derive validity_scope against the declared rayon; report out_of_scope distinctly from false, and scope_undeclared as a defect.
Derive validity_context from the preconditions and situation frame; report conditional_on_context vs unconditional.
Report the five statuses separately; never collapse them into one overall.
forbidden: collapsing the five axes into one overall status
reporting current_truth from the causal argument (or vice versa)
reporting a weak-validator pass as strong
assuming universality when scope is undeclared
reporting unconditional validity while an unmet precondition stands

steps: resolve the construct and its self-verifying spine
read the causal argument (pattern/behavior/algorithm) and derive causal_validity a-temporally
read the fresh health_assessment and derive current_truth for the current world
read the metric margin and observer-validation and derive validity_degree (evidence margin + validator strength)
read the declared scope and derive validity_scope (in/out-of-scope/undeclared)
read the preconditions and situation frame and derive validity_context
emit the five statuses as an orthogonal vector; refuse to collapse
run the independent observer and structured evaluation AST; derive this toolkit's own validity by the same five axes

content.authority: Graph-native CodeDefinition projection for the portable Validity toolkit; this JSON file is a materialized projection, not independent semantic authority.
content.model_note: This toolkit carries no atom circuit of its own; it is a model consumed by other constructs via DEPENDS_ON. Each consuming construct's health face reports one status per axis defined here.

content.honesty: Materialized and structurally shaped as a construct. Written BEFORE injection; after an injector commits it and consuming constructs are wired via DEPENDS_ON, this field reads stale. No construct's validity is derived by this model at runtime yet.

why: A single 'health' scalar hides real distinctions: a construct can be causally sound but currently false, or true now but unsound; collapsing them loses exactly what a reader needs.
Separating the strength and validity of the validators from the result prevents a weak or unproven validator from lending false confidence.
A declared scope keeps out-of-scope distinct from false, so a construct valid in its rayon is not mistaken for universally valid or wrongly failed.
Naming the context keeps conditional validity honest: a construct valid under an assumption is not reported as valid unconditionally.
Factoring this once, shared and consumed via DEPENDS_ON, keeps all constructs' validity comparable instead of each inventing its own health semantics.
rejected: one overall health scalar, because it conflates orthogonal axes
per-construct bespoke health semantics, because they become incomparable
assuming universal scope, because validity is always over some domain
reporting validator results without validator strength, because a weak pass is not a strong one

invariants: health is a vector over exactly five orthogonal axes
no axis is collapsed to hide another
causal_validity is derived independently of current_truth
validity_degree includes validator strength, not only the result
validity_scope reports out-of-scope distinctly from false
this toolkit is an instance of the model it defines

tests: detect an overall status that hid a red axis
detect current_truth derived from the causal argument
detect a weak-validator pass reported as strong
detect unconditional reported while a precondition is unmet
never convert a per-axis defect into an overall pass

content.independence: Reads a consuming construct's pattern/behavior/algorithm, its fresh health_assessment, its metric vector, its observer-validation result, its declared scope and its preconditions. It does not trust a construct's self-reported overall health.
checks: five orthogonal statuses present and separate
current_truth derived from fresh evidence only
validity_degree reflects margin AND validator strength
the toolkit reports its own validity by the same axes

content.note: Homoiconic: this toolkit reports ITS OWN health as the same five-axis vector it defines.
content.collapse_forbidden: No single overall health may hide a per-axis defect.
